findings.finding: The 2026-08-31 registered offering put 50,000,000 pre-split Class A shares (10.0m post-split, roughly 94% of the ~10.6m post-split Class A count) into public hands at a $0.75 post-split equivalent, with no lock-up disclosed in the closing 6-K, so at $1.25 those buyers still hold ~67% gains and can sell into any bounce during the 2026-10-05 session.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The shares are already registered (424B4 of 2026-08-28) and tradable; any bounce on 2026-10-05 meets this supply inside the window rather than later. It is a standing overhang, not a scheduled event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the offering closed, the stock fell -23.3% on 2026-05-28-type days repeatedly; within this name's own 12 comparable falls the median next close is -3.61% and 8 of 12 did not rise (baseline history). No direct prior reaction to this specific overhang is observable.
findings.why_not_priced: The fall has already erased most of the post-split run-up, but the price at $1.25 still sits well above the $0.75 cost basis of a holder base that is nearly the size of the float; if the overhang were fully spent the price would already be near or below $0.75. How much of the 10.0m has already been sold is unknown, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Short interest falling 90.8% to 56,867 shares by 2026-09-15 (https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/WCT/short-interest?assetclass=stocks) means there is no crowded short to cover into a bounce, which points the same way (no buyer of last resort).

outside_window.finding: Placement agent Prime Number Capital holds a 9-month right of first refusal on future offerings from 2026-08-31, making a further raise plausible but undated.
If the collapse continues below $1.00 for 30 business days, a Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency clock would start again (the company had one in 2025); at $1.25 it is not yet under $1.
